summary: Carbon County, WY lookout west of Keystone: 1911 telephone plan, 1930 steel tower, 1921 ranger staffing; listed gone, no site description today.

facts.design: 20-foot wooden platform per the listing; 1930 newspaper describes a steel tower
facts.status_note: Listed as gone; the sources give no removal date.

staffing.status: Used as a secondary lookout; district rangers manned it in hazardous fire periods

events.note: Telephone line planned to Jays Roost; a young man, Benj. Burch, was to be stationed there
District forest rangers served as lookouts on Jay's Roost during especially hazardous fire periods
New steel tower announced to replace the wooden tower; hauling bids taken
Steel tower placed on Jays Roost for use in hazardous weather

evidence.supports: Jays Roost is a mountain west of Keystone
evidence.quote: a mountain in the heart of the heavily timbered country west of Keystone

evidence.supports: Jays Roost is in Carbon County, Wyoming, and is listed as gone
evidence.quote: Jays Roost Carbon 41.16740 -106.33087 Platform Gone

evidence.supports: The site sits within the Medicine Bow National Forest
evidence.quote: Medicine Bow National Forest

evidence.supports: A telephone line was to be built to the site and a young man was to be stationed there (1911)
evidence.quote: A telephone line will be built to Jays roost, in connection with other lines, where young Mr. Benj. Burch will be stationed.

evidence.supports: Each station was to get a compass graduated in degrees
evidence.quote: Every station will be provided with a compass, marked in degrees.

evidence.supports: Stations compared bearings on a fire to work out where it lay
evidence.quote: The pointer is sited toward the fire and all stations in a position to see the fire are consulted

evidence.supports: The lookout listing describes a 20-foot wooden platform
evidence.quote: 20' wooden platform. Gone.

evidence.supports: In 1929 a new steel tower was to replace the wooden one
evidence.quote: A new steel lookout tower is to be erected by the forest service this spring, replacing the present wooden tower.

evidence.supports: Bids were being accepted to haul the new structure from the Foxpark railroad to the mountain
evidence.quote: Bids are now being accepted for the hauling of this tower from the railroad at Foxpark to Keystone and to the top of Jay's Roost mountain.

evidence.supports: In March 1930 a steel tower was placed on the mountain
evidence.quote: a steel tower was placed on Jays Roost

evidence.supports: Temporary observers could be posted there in bad weather
evidence.quote: will permit of temporary observers being placed at these points in the event of hazardous conditions.

evidence.supports: Smoke from the northwest clouded the view from the primary lookouts the season before
evidence.quote: Such conditions occurred last season when smoke from the northwest obscured the vision of the primary lookouts on Somber hill and Medicine Bow peak

evidence.supports: In 1921 district rangers served as lookouts on Jay's Roost, one of several secondary sites, in the most dangerous fire periods
evidence.quote: During especially hazardous fire periods, when the fire danger is most acute, the district forest rangers serve as lookouts on additional secondary lookouts on Jay's Roost

evidence.supports: The sources disagree on the structure on the summit at the end: a wooden platform in the listing, a steel tower in the 1930 article
evidence.quote: a steel tower was placed on Jays Roost

evidence.supports: The sources disagree on the structure on the summit at the end: a wooden platform in the listing
evidence.quote: 20' wooden platform. Gone.

evidence.supports: The telephone-line item is dated May 1911
The ranger-staffing item is dated May 1921
The steel-tower hauling item is dated June 1929
evidence.quote: June 9, 1929

evidence.supports: The steel-tower placement item is dated March 1930
evidence.quote: March 2, 1930

evidence.supports: The 1930 tower was for lookout facilities in particularly hazardous weather
evidence.quote: in case of particularly hazardous weather

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Rex's Fire Lookout Page listing gives a 20-foot wooden platform, while the 1929 and 1930 newspaper items describe a steel tower. The record does not say which structure was on the summit at the end, so the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Brief kind 'platform' matches the listing, but the 1930 steel tower is not in the brief's record. The 1930 article is credited to the Casper Tribune-Herald on westlookouts; the FFLOS Somber Hill page (firetower.org/lookouts/us/wy/somber-hill-lookout-site/) credits the same article to the Casper Star-Tribune, and the story cites westlookouts only. No removal date and no site-today description found; sites in this record were not described beyond the listing. Search budget: two websearch.py fallback queries; six page reads.
